crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software development grounds runtime implementation and compatibility debugging but not a dedicated browser-runtime profession boundary.

crosswalks.label: Web and Digital Interface Designers
crosswalks.rationale: Web interface work supplies adjacent browser/UI context while user-experience and design authority remain separate.

findings.summary: Browser runtime engineering sits between software implementation and web-interface contexts, making engine/version, synthetic-input and human-experience evidence boundaries essential.
findings.rationale: Research-first compilation makes the specialization boundary explicit before use.

gaps_against_body.description: Make single-engine success and synthetic/headless interaction separate from cross-browser and human/physical-use evidence.

nonclaims: No complete Browser Engineer reconstruction is claimed.
Occupational mappings are evidence, not profession identity.
No TEST/WORKING/CANON or adjacent authority is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: No adjacent professional, platform, security, product or institutional authority is created.
